item.title: A double-resonator coupler for high-fidelity two-qubit gates between superconducting qubits
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Residual ZZ interaction cancels completely outside straddling regime without direct qubit-qubit capacitive coupling using single-junction double-resonator coupler. Provides ∼70MHz activated ZZ interaction, enabling 20ns CZ gate with simulated coherent infidelity below 10−5.

Grade 0.476 · 1.8σ above the day's baseline · matched “Charge-insensitive qubit design derived from the Cooper pair box” · Seunghyeon Jin, Seungha Woo, Shinyoung Hwang, June-Young M. Lee, Jeongmin Shim, Sunje Kim, Dae Seok Han, Jaeho Shin, Eunjong Kim

Figure

Circuit and layout of transmon qubits coupled via the double-resonator coupler (a, b), mode coupling and flux-dependent single-excitation spectra (c, d), differential-mode potential wells (e), and mechanism of virtual-exchange path cancellation (f).

Asks

How to completely suppress residual ZZ interactions across flexible qubit-qubit frequency detunings without requiring multi-junction couplers or direct capacitive layout constraints?

Before

Single-transmon couplers require qubit detuning within straddling regime and direct qubit capacitance balancing; double-transmon and fluxonium couplers require multiple Josephson junctions.

But

Numerical simulation only. Evaluated using a 20-state basis with perturbative leakage corrections; dephasing assumes 1/f flux-noise amplitude Aφex=2π×10−6.

Tools

circuit quantization · instantaneous dressed-state time evolution · CMA-ES pulse optimization · Slepian-like flux pulse · quasi-static noise model

Abstract

Tunable couplers have enabled two-qubit gate fidelities in superconducting quantum processors to approach 99.9%, yet simultaneously suppressing residual interactions and maintaining flexible qubit-frequency allocation remain central challenges for scaling. Here, we propose a double-resonator coupler (DRC) consisting of two resonators interconnected by a single Josephson junction and a capacitor. The hybridized resonator modes provide two mediated exchange paths whose interference controls the qubit-qubit interaction. The DRC enables complete cancellation of residual ZZ interaction for qubit-qubit detunings well outside the straddling regime, even in the absence of direct qubit-qubit coupling, thereby relaxing constraints on frequency allocation and qubit placement. Away from the idle point, the same circuit provides a strong ZZ interaction of approximately 70 MHz, enabling a 20 ns controlled-Z gate with simulated coherent infidelity below 10⁻⁵. These results establish the DRC as a flexible single-junction coupler architecture for high-fidelity superconducting quantum processors.

item.title: Electrostatic splitting of an Edge Magnetoplasmon Resonator
item.description:
Long shot new result — Electrostatic splitting of an edge magnetoplasmon resonator yields RF transmission signatures for integer (ν=1,2) and fractional (ν=4/3,2/3) quantum Hall states, with cavity perimeter dropping to 17.5 μm past QPC pinch-off.

Grade 0.441 · 1.5σ above the day's baseline · matched “Circuit quantum electrodynamics” · Sloän Kouamé, Elric Frigerio, Giacomo Rebora, Suvankar Purkait, Yong Jin, Ulf Gennser, Antonella Cavanna, Jean-Marc Berroir, Emmanuel Baudin, Pascal Degiovanni, Franccois D. Parmentier, Gwendal Fève, Gerbold C. Ménard

Figure

Averaged RF transmission amplitude ⟨|Z|2⟩ plotted against QPC gate voltage VQPC and perpendicular magnetic field B. Peaks trace resonance trajectories for integer ν=1,2 and fractional ν=4/3,2/3 Hall plateaus across the QPC pinch-off transition.

Asks

How does polarizing an embedded quantum point contact influence edge magnetoplasmon modes and cavity geometry in a quantum Hall resonator?

But

Aharonov-Bohm interference oscillations not observed due to small expected period; ν=2/3 center field was beyond maximum accessible magnetic field (B>8 T).

Tools

AlGaAs/GaAs 2DEG · RF lock-in reflectometry and transmission · electrostatic quantum point contacts · cryogenic dilution refrigerator (30 mK)

Abstract

Edge-magnetoplasmon resonators have been proposed as a powerful tool to detect anyons by introducing a quantum point contact into an isolated quantum Hall system probed via radiofrequency radiation. In this paper, we study the effect of a quantum point contact embedded within an edge-magnetoplasmon resonator and how its polarization influences the propagating magnetoplasmonic mode. Combining dc and rf measurements, we unambiguously evidence the signature of both integer (ν= 1 and 2) and fractional quantum Hall states (ν= 4/3 and 2/3) within the radiofrequency transmission signal. Using electrostatic gating, we determine the physical parameters characterizing the electrostatic edge of an AlGaAs/GaAs based two-dimensional electron gas. We extract the dependence of the cavity perimeter with the gate voltage of the quantum point contact and fully characterize the path followed by edge magnetoplasmons in this system. Finally, we provide a geometric model in good agreement with experimental results.

item.title: TETRIS-Q: Tiling-based Effective Transient-fault Reduction on Interleaved Superconducting Qubits
item.description:
Long shot new method — Combining substrate phonon barrier tiling with QEC interleaving reduces peak logical error rate by over 99.8% and shortens transient duration by 80% under simulated radiation strikes. Sparser multi-qubit tiling cuts barrier fabrication perimeter cost by up to 87% with minimal performance loss.

Grade 0.437 · 1.4σ above the day's baseline · matched “Superconducting Qubits: Current State of Play” · Marzio Vallero, Gioele Casagranda, Flavio Vella, Paolo Rech

Figure

Heatmap of average logical error rate for a distance-7 rotated surface code across tile sizes (1 to 16 qubits) and numbers of interleaved codes (1 to 9) at barrier permeability bp=0.1.

Asks

Can substrate-level phonon barrier tiling and quantum error correction code interleaving mitigate radiation-induced spatially correlated faults in superconducting quantum chips without execution overhead?

But

Numerical simulation only (51 million circuit simulations) using rotated surface codes under a parametrizable barrier permeability model (bp).

Tools

TETRIS-Q planar-mesh tiling algorithm · rotated surface code simulation · substrate-level phonon barrier model · QEC code interleaving

Abstract

The struggle of the hour in quantum computing research is achieving effective suppression of the error mechanisms induced by the interaction of external radiation with superconducting quantum devices. Despite the rapid advancements in quantum error correction (QEC) of recent years, radiation-induced faults are yet to be fully addressed. These events are known to be the cause of simultaneous correlated defects in qubits that lie onto a single substrate, ultimately jeopardising QEC code effectiveness. In this paper, we propose to selectively combine substrate-level phonon barriers and QEC interleaving via a planar-mesh tiling algorithm, TETRIS-Q, reaching efficient and effective suppression of radiation events. Our cross-layer solution comes at no extra cost in terms of QEC code execution or decoding time. We model and simulate radiation-induced transient faults over a plethora of barrier and QEC interleaving configurations. Through more than 51 million quantum circuit simulations, we show peak logical error reductions of more than 99.8 %, together with an 80% reduction of the observable transient duration with permeable barriers. We find that sparser tiling can reach comparable performance to single qubit tiling, prompting cost reductions of upwards of 87 % in barrier tracing. By leveraging independent QEC code interleaving, we measure up to one order of magnitude average logical error rate reductions without the use of permeable barriers, and up to three orders of magnitude with the joint usage of barriers.
